newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to use drug money for public housing.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to use drug money for public housing.

text.p: The Colombian government said on Friday that it plans to use part of the money and assets it confiscates from the country's billionaire drug lords to build low-income housing.
The decision was announced in a decree issued by President Ernesto Samper under terms of the state of economic emergency the government declared on Jan. 13 to fight its burgeoning fiscal deficit.
A so-called asset forfeiture law allowing for the seizure of all assets and properties linked to Colombia's criminal drug syndicates was approved by the country's Congress in December.

Estimates vary widely as to how much the government could raise through the seizures, but the respected weekly news magazine Semana estimates that Colombia's top drug lords are worth a combined total of $200 billion.
Up to 50 percent of seized assets, and 20 percent of seized property, will be used to finance low income housing projects, according to Friday's decree.
